coverageArticles.headline: What to Know About Friday’s Nationwide Ground Stop
coverageArticles.description: The air traffic control system’s overloaded, antiquated telecommunications equipment sustained its latest widespread failure, prompting a call for more money to fuel faster upgrades.

coverageArticles.headline: How to Land 4,000 Planes During a Ground Stop
coverageArticles.description: For four and a half hours, the sky above the United States emptied out. Normally, throughout the day and the night, thousands of planes are taking off, crisscrossing the country, and landing.

coverageArticles.headline: Scenes From the Nationwide Ground Stop
coverageArticles.description: On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare ground stop at all U.S. airports, citing “extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.” Across the country, departing flights were held for hours before the stop—attributed to a telecommunications outage—was lifted, disrupting travel plans for some 1.5 million people.

coverageArticles.headline: FAA ends hours-long nationwide ground stop
coverageArticles.description: The FAA lifted its nationwide ground stop Friday night after hours of chaos and thousands of delays and cancellations. Why it matters: The effects of the rare and extreme move will likely ripple through the weekend, with travelers stranded and airlines' planes and crews out of position.

coverageArticles.headline: FAA lifts rare nationwide ground stop
coverageArticles.description: The FAA on Friday lifted a rare nationwide ground stop that impacted more than 14,500 flights after a major outage affecting the US’ air communications system. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed “an incredibly old air traffic control system,” and said the government didn’t suspect any nefarious causes, such as a terrorist or cyber attack.

coverageArticles.headline: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop that blocked takeoffs for hours
coverageArticles.description: A view of an information board at the Chicago O'Hare International Airport, filled with waiting passengers on November 13, 2026. Photo by Jacek Boczarski/Anadolu via Getty Images) | Anadolu via Getty Images Takeoffs from airports throughout the US largely stopped on Friday after the FAA issued a national ground stop at 3:44PM ET "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."

coverageArticles.headline: Duffy details timeline of ground stop, demands more FAA funding
coverageArticles.description: Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy gives the timeline of the paralyzing FAA ground stop, which left travelers across the country stranded for hours. Duffy says the issue was due to old communications systems.

coverageArticles.headline: Of Course Americans Blamed the Ground Stop on AI
coverageArticles.description: For many hours, the Federal Aviation Administration did not explain why it issued a national ground stop in the United States this afternoon. The agency described the cause only as a “ telecommunications outage ” and cited “ extraordinary circumstances ,” but failed to say more. So speculation abounded: Was the problem connected with the onboarding of a new AI route-selection system this week?

coverageArticles.headline: Airport Chaos Began Long Before the Ground Stop
coverageArticles.description: Every civilian airplane in the United States has been told not to fly, owing to a nationwide FAA ground stop. As I write this, very little is known about the nature of the safety risk or the issue underlying it.

coverageArticles.headline: Stranded passenger in Las Vegas on nationwide ground stop: "Nobody has answers"
coverageArticles.description: Clara Pablo was trying to get home from Las Vegas to New York on Friday when the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop. She joined CBS News' to share her experience. Then, CBS Atlanta's Nakell Williams reports on the scene from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport.

coverageArticles.headline: FAA issues rare nationwide ground stop due to 'extraordinary circumstances'
coverageArticles.description: Air travel across the country came to a standstill on Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop citing "extraordinary circumstances" and "reasons of safety." Aviation correspondent Miles O'Brien reports.

coverageArticles.headline: Update to network connecting air traffic control system led to outage before ground stop, sources ay
coverageArticles.description: An update to the private communications network that connects America's air traffic control system caused the system to reboot, leading to a crash and a communications outage, multiple sources told CBS News. Lindsey Reiser anchors continuing coverage.

coverageArticles.headline: Flight Canceled During the FAA Ground Stop? Here’s What to Do.
coverageArticles.description: Travelers are entitled to a refund if your flight is canceled, regardless of the reason, or if a flight is significantly delayed or changed and you decide not to take it.

coverageArticles.headline: FAA has lifted its third-ever nationwide ground stop
coverageArticles.description: The Federal Administration lifted its third-ever nationwide ground stop after several hours Friday evening. Domestic flights were cleared to begin taking off at 8:35 pm EST. FAA Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy cautioned that, barring massive system updates, there will be "more of these" ahead.

coverageArticles.headline: Some airports beginning to run out of space for planes amid nationwide ground stop
coverageArticles.description: A source with knowledge of the situation told NBC News that Reagan National Airport is at capacity and that Chicago O’Hare is nearing capacity, meaning there is no place for planes to park and that some of the planes may have to divert to other airports.

coverageArticles.headline: No indication of nefarious attack before FAA ground stop, Mullin says
coverageArticles.description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Friday's FAA ground stop was caused by a telecommunications outage and there is currently no indication of a nefarious attack. Major Garrett anchors ongoing coverage.

coverageArticles.headline: DHS head Markwayne Mullin says there is not a threat to the U.S. amid FAA ground stop
coverageArticles.description: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin spoke to at the White House on Friday afternoon after the FAA issues a total ground stop. NPR was there for the briefing.

coverageArticles.headline: Stuck on the tarmac without information: Travelers share their ground stop experiences
coverageArticles.description: Passengers stuck on airplanes on tarmacs across the country during the FAA ground stop on Friday share their stories.

coverageArticles.headline: Secy. Mullin says FAA ground stop was caused by 'telecommunication outage'
coverageArticles.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters the nationwide ground stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration was the result of a telecommunication outage. He also assured that the issue was the result of some for of attack or hack.

coverageArticles.headline: Ground stop ordered for all airports nationwide for ‘reasons of safety’
coverageArticles.description: The Federal Aviation Administration said Friday that it was halting all departing flights “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.”
